Blocks.Text: The verificationUrl is a dynamic link that directs members to complete identity or workplace verification on LinkedIn before returning to your application. It serves as the primary mechanism for resolving unverified states and for prompting members to re-verify when existing verifications no longer satisfy a requested freshness requirement.
The /verificationReport API may return a verificationUrl when:

A member has not completed all available verifications.
A member has completed only some available verifications.
A member has existing verifications that are older than the requested verifiedWithinDays freshness window.

Your application should use this URL to redirect the member to LinkedIn so they can complete verification. Once verification is completed, call /verificationReport again to retrieve the updated status.
This step is critical to the integration flow, ensuring eligible members are prompted to verify rather than remaining unverified.

SectionPath: Why the Verification URL Is Important
Blocks.Text: If your application only reads verification status but never surfaces the verification URL, many eligible members will remain unverified because they are never prompted to start the verification flow.

Blocks.Text: Your application should use this URL to redirect the member to LinkedIn.
When the member selects "Verify on LinkedIn", redirect them to the verificationUrl.
After successfully completing verification on LinkedIn, the member can be automatically redirected back to your application if a valid redirectUri is provided.

The redirectUri must exactly match one of the Authorized Redirect URLs configured in your LinkedIn Developer Portal
The redirectUri parameter must be URL encoded before appending to the verificationUrl
If the redirect configuration is invalid or missing, the member will remain on LinkedIn after verification and must manually return to your application.

Your app redirects the member to the verificationUrl

Your app calls /verificationReport again to retrieve updated verification data
Your app resumes the member's session and displays updated verification state

If you want the member to return to your application after completing verification, append the redirectUri parameter to the verificationUrl, making sure that the redirectUri value is URL-encoded before appending.

Go to LinkedIn Developer Portal
Select your application then navigate to Auth tab
Under Authorized redirect URLs, add your redirect URI
Save changes
The redirectUri must exactly match a URL registered in your LinkedIn Developer App's Auth tab.
LinkedIn validates the redirectUri against the Authorized Redirect URLs configured in your LinkedIn Developer Portal.
Validation requires an exact match of:

Protocol (for example, https)
Domain
Path
Any pre-registered query parameters
Wildcard or prefix matching is not supported.
The only exception is the OAuth 2.0 state parameter, which may vary per request and is ignored during validation.
The OAuth 2.0 state parameter is the only supported dynamic query parameter.
Partners may append a state parameter to their redirectUri at runtime:

Does not need to be pre-registered
Is ignored during redirect URL validation
Is preserved and passed through to the final redirect URL after verification
If no state parameter is provided, the redirect URL is used as registered.
Query parameters other than state must be included in the registered redirect URL and must match exactly at runtime.
These examples fail because query parameters other than state differ from the registered URL.
Automatic redirection back to your application will not occur in the following scenarios:

The provided redirectUri does not exactly match a URL registered in the LinkedIn Developer Portal
The redirectUri parameter is missing
The redirectUri parameter is empty
The redirectUri value is not URL encoded correctly
Additional query parameters (other than state) are present and do not match the registered URL

The member will remain on the LinkedIn verification page after verification
The member must manually return to your application
Your application should handle this gracefully and instruct the member to return
